notes.44v.a.1: Ivy 'that grows on the ground' (44v.a.6-7) may be ground ivy. 'nât' (44v.a.13), 'seam', taken as the suture of the skull. 'daz halpteil' (44v.a.12) could also mean 'a half part'.

nodes.text: Here begins the book on the natural faculty.
Here begins the medicine book of Hippocrates, which
he wrote against all the diseases that
can arise in the whole human
body. For headache:
take wormwood, rue, ivy that grows on the
ground, and pound it with honey, and
mix it with the white of an egg; lay it on
a cloth and bind the head with it.
Take peach kernels and pound them with
rose oil, or with plain oil;
add half as much sharp vinegar to it.
Anoint the whole head with it, up to the suture.
If it seems to you that your head is about to split
from the pain, then pound the ivy and
mix oil with it, and press it through a
cloth, and anoint the forehead with what runs out
of it. It will help you very well. Take rose
and celandine, and pound them with vinegar,
and anoint the head with it. Take the seed
of the nettle, pound it with vinegar, and
anoint the head with it. With all these
the headache is driven away.
For falling hair:
burn linseed and mix it
with oil, and anoint the hair. Burn a ram's
pot, until it boils down to two beakers
full, and give it to him to drink for three days;
then the stone breaks. Likewise: take the egg that
was laid on a Thursday, and give
it to him to drink with wine. For dysentery
that discharges blood: take plantain
roots, and lovage, and chervil
